title: Change Log
description: Full change log for the Assemble design system
content:
Change Log

All notable changes to the Assemble design system are documented here. This log tracks updates across tokens, components, documentation, and tooling.

Versioning follows Semantic Versioning. For major announcements, see the Releases page.

[0.9.5] — 2026-03-10

Added
McChatCard component for conversation-style card layouts
McStatCard component for metric and statistic displays
McNbaWidget for next-best-action recommendation cards
Claude Code skills package for AI-assisted Flutter development
Documentation site with Astro — foundations, components, patterns, and guides
Figma MCP integration guide for Claude Code

Changed
Updated McButton pressed state to use correct state layer opacity (10%)
Improved McSideSheet animation timing for smoother transitions
Refined dark theme surface gradient stops for better visual hierarchy

Fixed
McTextField focus ring not matching the correct outline color in high contrast modes
McChip text truncation on small screens
Spacing token space-600 resolving to wrong value in medium contrast themes

[0.9.0] — 2026-01-15

Added
Initial Material 3 design token set in OKLCH color space
Six theme variants: light, dark, medium contrast, high contrast
33+ Flutter components in the Pegasus library
McAfee extended color tokens (brand, positive, warning, mcafee-red)
Surface gradient tokens (high, moderate, low energy)
Glass-radial and border gradient tokens
Typography scale: display, headline, title, body, label at all sizes
Spacing scale from 100 (4px) through 1200
State layer tokens for hover, focus, pressed, dragged
Figma libraries synced with token pipeline
CSS custom properties export via build-tokens.js

Changed
Migrated from legacy McAfee color palette to Material 3 tonal palette system

[0.8.1] — 2025-11-20

Added
McSearchBar component
McFilterChipGroup for multi-select chip sets
McMultiFeatureList for complex list layouts
McConnectionDetails component for network/device info display

Changed
McCard now supports custom content slots via McCustomCard
McLoader animation updated for smoother rendering on low-end devices

Fixed
McBottomNavbar badge count not updating dynamically
McAppBar title alignment issue on iOS

[0.8.0] — 2025-10-01

Added
Initial Pegasus Flutter component library
McApp, McScaffold, McAppBar — app shell components
McButton — filled, outlined, text, and icon variants
McCard, McHorizontalCard — card layouts
McTextField — text input with validation states
McChip, McFilterChip, McListChip — chip components
McCarousel — horizontal scrolling content
McBadge, McDivider, McModal — display utilities
McLoader, McProgressIndicator, McSkeletonLoading — loading states
McBottomNavbar, McSideSheet, McMenu — navigation components
McList, McListItem, McFeaturedListItem — list components
McChatBubble, McChatPrompt, McAIBubble — chat components
mcfluttertokens package with color, typography, spacing, and elevation tokens

Tracking changes

This change log is maintained alongside the Assemble GitHub repository. Each tagged release includes:
Updated token files in /tokens
Updated pegasusflutter package version
Updated mcflutter_tokens package version
Updated documentation and Figma libraries

To track changes in real time, watch the repository or subscribe to release notifications on GitHub.

title: Claude + Pegasus Kit
description: Set up Claude Code to build Flutter UIs with McAfee's Pegasus design system
content:
Claude + Pegasus Kit

Configure Claude Code to build Flutter UIs using only McAfee's Pegasus design system — no raw Material widgets, no hardcoded colors, no manual styling.

What it does

The Pegasus Claude Kit drops a set of configuration files into your Flutter project that instruct Claude Code to:
Use McApp instead of MaterialApp
Use McButton, McCard, McTextField, McScaffold, etc. instead of raw Material widgets
Map all colors to context.extendedColors or Theme.of(context).colorScheme
Map all typography to context.typographyTokens
Map all spacing and border radius to context.spacingTokens
Map all elevation/shadows to context.elevations
Never hardcode any visual values

Every line of Flutter UI code Claude generates will be fully on-brand.

What's included

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| CLAUDE.md | Project-level instructions Claude reads on startup |
| .claude/skills/SKILL.md | Deep component & token reference with every Pegasus API |
| .claude/settings.local.json | Pre-configured permissions for flutter commands |
| FIGMASETUP.md | Guide for connecting Figma designs to Claude via MCP |
| templates/ | Starter pubspec.yaml deps, lint rules, and main.dart |
| examples/chat-app/ | Full working example app built with Pegasus |
| setup.sh | Automated installation script |

Prerequisites

Before you begin, make sure you have:
Flutter SDK 3.0+ installed
Claude Code installed (npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code)
Access to the McAfee GitHub org (for pegasusflutter and mcfluttertokens)

Installation

Option A — Automated setup (recommended)

If you have the Assemble repo cloned, run the setup script from your Flutter project directory:

Or pass your project path as an argument:

The script will:
Copy CLAUDE.md to your project root
Copy the .claude/ directory (skills + permissions)
Copy FIGMASETUP.md for optional Figma integration
Check your pubspec.yaml for Pegasus dependencies

Option B — Manual setup

Step 1 — Copy Claude configuration files

Step 2 — Add Pegasus dependencies to pubspec.yaml

Step 3 — Install packages

Step 4 — Start Claude Code

Claude will now follow the Pegasus design system for every UI request.

Verify it's working

Open Claude Code in your project and ask it to generate a simple screen:

"Create a settings screen with a side menu containing Home, Profile, and Notifications"

The output should:
✅ Use McApp as the app root
✅ Use McScaffold and McAppBar for layout
✅ Use McSideSheet for the side menu
✅ Use McSideSheetItem for navigation items
✅ Use context.typographyTokens for text styles
✅ Use context.extendedColors or colorScheme for colors
❌ No MaterialApp, Scaffold, AppBar, Drawer, hardcoded colors, or raw TextStyle

Figma integration (optional)

You can connect Figma to Claude Code so it reads your designs directly and generates Pegasus Flutter code from frames.

One-time setup:

Authenticate: start Claude Code, type /mcp, find figma, select Authenticate, and allow access in the browser.

Usage: paste a Figma frame link into Claude Code along with your request:

See FIGMASETUP.md (included in the kit) for the full guide, troubleshooting, and rate limit details.

Prompting guide

Once installed, you can prompt Claude naturally. It handles all component and token selection automatically.

For developers

"Build a home dashboard showing VPN protection status, recent threat chips, and a connect button."

"Create an onboarding screen with a headline, subtext, and a next button."

"Build a form with email and password fields and a sign-in button."

For designers & PMs

Describe the screen's purpose and content — Claude handles everything:

"Make a settings screen with a side menu containing Home, Profile, and Notifications."

"Build a custom status card with a green background and body text for 'all clear' state."

With Figma

Component quick reference

These are the Pegasus components Claude will use. You never need to memorize these — Claude picks the right one automatically.

| Need | Pegasus component |
|---|---|
| App root | McApp |
| Screen layout | McScaffold |
| Top bar | McAppBar |
| Button | McButton |
| Card / container | McCard |
| Text input | McTextField |
| Chip / tag / status | McChip |
| Side menu / drawer | McSideSheet.show() |
| Nav item | McSideSheetItem |
| Badge / count | McBadge |
| Status / connection info | McConnectionDetails |

Token quick reference

| Need | Token |
|---|---|
| Brand / semantic colors | Theme.of(context).colorScheme. |
| McAfee brand colors | context.extendedColors.mcafee / .positive / .warning |
| Button colors | context.buttonColors. |
| Gradients | context.gradientColors.* |
| Corner radius / spacing | context.spacingTokens.cornerMedium |
| Typography / text styles | context.typographyTokens.bodyMedium |
| Elevation / shadows | context.elevations["2"] |
| Tonal palette | context.tonalPalettes.brand.tone40 |

Example app

The kit includes a complete chat UI built entirely with Pegasus. Run it to see the design system in action:

This example demonstrates McApp, McScaffold, McAppBar, McSideSheet, McButton, McTextField, McChip, McBadge, and full token usage for colors, typography, spacing, and elevation.

Updating

To update Pegasus package versions, change the ref: values in your pubspec.yaml:

Then run flutter pub get.

To update the Claude configuration files, re-run the setup script or copy the latest versions from the Assemble repo.

Troubleshooting

Claude is generating raw Material widgets
Your CLAUDE.md or .claude/skills/SKILL.md may be missing. Verify both files exist in your project root and re-run the setup script if needed.

flutter pub get fails on Pegasus packages
Make sure you have access to the McAfee GitHub org. Try authenticating with:

Colors/tokens not applying
Ensure your app root uses McApp, not MaterialApp. McApp auto-configures the theme from design tokens.

"No MaterialLocalizations found" error
McSideSheet.show() must be called from within an McApp widget tree. Check your widget hierarchy.

Need to explore available components
Run the Pegasus Widgetbook for interactive docs:

title: Color
description: Color system, palettes, and usage guidelines for the Assemble design system
content:
Color

Color brings meaning, hierarchy, and personality to interfaces. Assemble's color system is built on Material 3 color roles and extended with McAfee brand colors to create consistent, accessible experiences.

Color roles

Material 3 organizes color into semantic roles rather than fixed values. Each role has a specific purpose in the UI.

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

Surface hierarchy

Surfaces use container tokens to create depth without relying on elevation shadows. Toggle your theme to see how each surface adapts.

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

Brand colors

Beyond the standard Material 3 palette, Assemble includes McAfee-specific color extensions.

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

Gradients

Assemble provides gradient tokens for expressive surfaces and interactive elements.

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

Color space

All web tokens are defined in the OKLCH color space, providing perceptually uniform color manipulation. Contrast ratios and perceived lightness stay consistent across the palette.

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

Dark mode

Colors adapt automatically between light and dark themes. The semantic token names stay the same — only the underlying palette values shift. Use the theme toggle in the top bar to see these swatches update live.

 
 
 
 
 
 

Apply themes using the data-theme attribute:

```html
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

Never rely on color alone to convey meaning. Pair color with text labels, icons, or patterns so information remains accessible to all users.

Accordions display collapsible content panels for organizing and revealing information progressively. They reduce visual clutter by hiding secondary content until needed.

 
 
 
 
 

Installation

title: Alert Banner
description: Alert Banner component usage and guidelines
content:
Alert Banner

A compact, dismissable alert banner for short messages anchored to the top or bottom of a region. Use for informational messages with an optional action link — for example "Trial ends in 11 days" with a "View plans" action.

 
 
 
 

Installation

Modes

Neutral

The default mode. Transparent surface with a 1px on-surface-variant border.

Info

Secondary fill with on-secondary content. Use for informational messages.

Critical

Error fill with on-secondary content. Use for urgent or error messages.

Positive

Extended-positive fill with on-secondary content. Use for success confirmations.

Status

Extended-attention fill with on-secondary content. Use for warnings or status updates.

Custom Icon

Override the default notificationimportant icon with any Material Symbols name.

Without Close Button

Omit the close button for persistent banners.

Guidelines
Keep banner titles concise — one line preferred
Use the action link for a clear next step (e.g. "View plans", "Renew now")
Use neutral for general messages, critical only for genuinely urgent issues
The banner auto-wraps long text; the action link flows inline on the second line
Always provide a close mechanism unless the banner is truly permanent

API

Web

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|----------|------|---------|-------------|
| title | string | '' | Headline text shown right of the icon |
| mode | neutral \| info \| critical \| positive \| status | neutral | Visual mode controlling colors |
| icon | string | notificationimportant | Leading Material Symbols icon name |
| action-label | string | '' | Action link text. Empty = no link |
| show-close | boolean | true | Whether the close button is shown |
| close-label | string | Dismiss | Accessible label for close button |

Events:
| Event | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| action | Fired when the action link is clicked |
| close | Fired when the close button is clicked |

Flutter

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| title | String | required | Headline text |
| mode | AsmAlertBannerMode | .neutral | Visual mode |
| icon | IconData | Icons.notification_important | Leading icon |
| actionLabel | String? | null | Action link text |
| onActionPressed | VoidCallback? | null | Action handler |
| onClosePressed | VoidCallback? | null | Close handler. null hides the button |
| closeSemanticLabel | String | 'Dismiss' | Accessible label for close |
| semanticLabel | String? | null | Override announced text |

title: Button
description: Button component usage and guidelines
content:
Button

Buttons allow users to take actions and make choices with a single tap. Use buttons to communicate actions users can take throughout the UI in dialogs, forms, cards, and toolbars.

A live Flutter build of the button, rendered with AsmButton from pegasus_flutter. Each preview below is a live Flutter demo; switch the code tab to Web to see the web component equivalent.

Usage

Use a button whenever the user needs to trigger an action or make a choice — submit a form, confirm a dialog, apply a filter. To navigate to a new URL, use a link instead of a button.

Variants

Filled

The default high-emphasis button for primary actions. Use sparingly to highlight the most important action on the page.

Tonal

A softer emphasis button for secondary actions. Uses the surface container color with on-surface text.

Text

A low-emphasis button for less prominent actions. No background, just label text.

Outline

A medium-emphasis button with a border. Use for secondary actions alongside a filled button.

Sizes

Buttons come in four sizes. Use large as the standard size.

Destructive

Add destructive for dangerous or irreversible actions. Supported on filled, tonal, and text variants.

With icons

Use start-icon and end-icon attributes with any Material Symbols icon name.

Anatomy

| Part | Description | Required |
|------|-------------|----------|
| Container | Background, border and radius resolved from the variant; padding resolved from the size | Yes |
| Label | The label text, rendered semibold | Yes |
| Leading icon | Material Symbols glyph set via start-icon (web) / startIcon (Flutter) | No |
| Trailing icon | Material Symbols glyph set via end-icon (web) / endIcon (Flutter) | No |
| State layer | Hover / pressed overlay tinted per variant | On interaction |
| Focus ring | 2px outline shown on :focus-visible | On focus |

Behavior & States

Every variant responds to the same interaction states. Disabled buttons are removed from the tab order and suppress all pointer and keyboard activation.

| Variant | Default | Hover | Pressed | Focus | Disabled |
|---------|---------|-------|---------|-------|----------|
| filled | Primary background, on-primary label | + hover overlay | + pressed overlay | Focus ring | Reduced opacity, no pointer events |
| tonal | Surface-container background | + hover overlay | + pressed overlay | Focus ring | Reduced opacity, no pointer events |
| text | Transparent, primary label | Subtle overlay | Stronger overlay | Focus ring | Reduced opacity, no pointer events |
| outline | Transparent, 1px outline | + hover overlay | + pressed overlay | Focus ring | Reduced opacity, no pointer events |

Adding destructive swaps the color role to the error palette while keeping the same state behavior.

Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| Enter | Activate the button |
| Space | Activate the button |
| Tab | Move focus to the next focusable element |
| Shift + Tab | Move focus to the previous focusable element |

Accessibility

| Requirement | Implementation |
|-------------|----------------|
| Accessible name | label (web) — or semanticLabel on Flutter to override the spoken name |
| Element | Native button semantics on both platforms — never a div with a click handler |
| Keyboard | Enter and Space activate the button |
| Focus | Visible focus ring via :focus-visible |
| Disabled | disabled (web) / onPressed: null (Flutter) removes the button from the tab order |
| Touch target | Minimum 44×44px hit area |
| Icon-only usage | Provide semanticLabel / aria-label and a tooltip describing the action |
| Destructive | Pair with a confirmation step for irreversible actions |

Guidelines
Use clear, concise labels that describe the action
Place the primary action button on the right in dialogs
Avoid using too many buttons in one view
Use filled buttons sparingly to emphasize the most important action
Use the destructive option only for irreversible actions like delete

Choosing a variant

Anti-patterns
Don't place two filled buttons side by side — pair filled with tonal or outline.
Don't ship a button with no accessible name — always supply label (or semanticLabel for icon-only).
Don't run a destructive action without confirmation when it can't be undone.
Don't invent variants — only filled, tonal, text, and outline exist on the web component.
Don't build a button from a div — use asm-button / AsmButton for correct semantics.

API

Web

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|----------|------|---------|-------------|
| label | string | '' | The button label text |
| variant | filled \| tonal \| text \| outline | filled | The visual style |
| size | huge \| spacious \| default \| compact | default | The button size |
| disabled | boolean | false | Whether the button is disabled |
| destructive | boolean | false | Destructive/danger mode |
| start-icon | string | '' | Material Symbols icon name before label |
| end-icon | string | '' | Material Symbols icon name after label |

Flutter

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| label | String | required | The button label text |
| automationIdentifier | String | required | Stable id used for test automation |
| onPressed | VoidCallback? | null | Tap handler. null disables the button |
| startIcon | Widget? | null | Leading icon widget |
| endIcon | Widget? | null | Trailing icon widget |
| variant | AsmButtonVariant | .text | The visual style (filled, tonal, text, textNoPadding, ghost, outline, strictBlack, strictWhite) |
| size | AsmButtonSize | .large | The button size (large, medium, small, xsmall) |
| destructive | bool | false | Destructive/danger mode |
| semanticLabel | String? | null | Overrides the accessible label |
| tooltip | String? | null | Optional tooltip text |

Contract

Machine-readable contract for AI agents and the component registry. This mirrors the real asm-button / AsmButton surface documented above — keep it in sync when the API changes.

title: Calendar
description: Calendar component usage and guidelines
content:
Calendar

An inline date/date-range picker following the Figma Calendar design. Supports single-date and range selection modes, with optional action buttons and full/grid-only chrome variants.

 
 

Installation

Single Date

Picks one date. The selected day uses primary background with on-primary text.

Range Selection

Picks a start + end date pair. Endpoints use secondary fill, and the span between is highlighted at 30% opacity.

Chrome Variants

Full Chrome

Renders with card background, title, rounded corners (12px), and shadow.

Grid Only

Bare date grid for embedding inside a parent surface (e.g. inside a date input dropdown).

Action Buttons

Cancel / OK

Clear / Cancel / OK

With Min/Max Constraints

Disable dates outside a specific range.

Guidelines
Use the calendar for date selection where visual context matters (booking, scheduling)
Pair with asm-date-input for inline editing with a dropdown picker
Use grid-only chrome when embedding inside another surface
Provide min-date / max-date to prevent invalid selections
Use range mode for booking flows requiring start and end dates
Today's date always shows a primary-colored border ring

API

Web

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|----------|------|---------|-------------|
| mode | single \| range | single | Selection mode |

description: Carousel indicator component usage and guidelines
content:
Carousel Indicator

A row of dots indicating the current page in a carousel or onboarding flow. Purely presentational — the caller controls the active index.

 
 

Installation

Default

Various Counts

Guidelines
Use below carousel or paged content to indicate position
Keep the page count reasonable (3–10 dots)

Icon Button

Icon buttons help people take supplementary actions with a single tap. Use icon buttons for compact actions like toggling a favorite, opening a menu, or performing a delete.

 
 
 
 
 

Installation

Variants

Standard

The default icon button with no background. Ideal for toolbar actions and less prominent controls.

Filled

High-emphasis icon button with a solid background. Use for primary icon actions.

Tonal

A softer emphasis icon button. Uses the surface container color for a subtler appearance.

Outline

A medium-emphasis icon button with a border. Use alongside filled icon buttons for secondary actions.

Sizes

Icon buttons come in four sizes. Use default as the standard size.

Destructive

Add destructive for dangerous or irreversible actions.

Toggle

Use the selected attribute to indicate a toggled state, such as a bookmarked or favorited item.

Guidelines
Always provide a label for accessibility — icon buttons have no visible text
Use selected for toggle states like bookmark, favorite, or pin
Use destructive only for irreversible actions like delete
Prefer standard variant for toolbars to reduce visual noise
Provide a tooltip in Flutter for hover/long-press discoverability

title: Theming
description: Understanding the Assemble theming system based on Material 3
content:
Theming

Assemble's theming system is built on the Material 3 design system. It provides a comprehensive set of design tokens that adapt across six theme variants, ensuring consistent visual experiences across Android, iOS, and macOS products.

Theme variants

The design system supports two theme modes:

| Theme | Description |
|---|---|
| Light | Default light appearance for standard viewing conditions |
| Dark | Default dark appearance for low-light environments |

Each variant is defined as a complete token set in the repository under /tokens/modes/assemble/:

How theming works

Tokens are structured in two layers:
Material reference tokens (md.ref.palette.) — The base color palette containing tonal values from 0–100 for each color role (primary, secondary, tertiary, error, neutral, brand)
Mode-specific semantic tokens (md.sys.color.) — Map palette values to semantic roles (surface, on-surface, primary-container, etc.) based on the active theme

When a theme is applied, the semantic tokens resolve to different palette stops. For example, md.sys.color.primary maps to palette.primary40 in light mode but palette.primary80 in dark mode.

Extended tokens

Beyond the standard Material 3 color roles, Assemble includes McAfee-specific extensions:
Brand colors — McAfee red, brand primary, and container variants
Extended semantic colors — Positive (green), warning/attention (amber), and McAfee accent
Surface gradients — High, moderate, and low energy gradient sets with three stops each
Glass effects — Radial glass-blur gradient tokens
Action gradients — Interactive element gradient stops
Border gradients — Decorative gradient borders
Shadow tokens — Elevation-based shadow definitions

Web (CSS)

Apply themes using the data-theme attribute on the root element:

Available values: light, dark

All CSS custom properties update automatically when the theme changes:

Flutter (Android & iOS)

In Flutter, theming is managed through McApp, which applies the correct token set based on the platform's current appearance:

Access theme-aware colors in any widget:

Platform behavior

Android

Android uses the system-level dark mode toggle to switch between light and dark base themes.

The Pegasus McApp widget detects these settings automatically and applies the corresponding token set.

iOS

iOS follows the same light/dark mode system toggle.

McApp reads the MediaQuery accessibility flags and selects the appropriate theme variant.

macOS

McAfee products on macOS integrate with the native macOS appearance settings:
Appearance — Follows the system light/dark mode setting (System Preferences → Appearance)

macOS products use the system accessibility API to detect these preferences and map them to the corresponding Assemble theme variant. This ensures McAfee desktop products feel native without requiring manual theme selection.

Color space

All color tokens use the OKLCH color space for web and are stored as hex values in the token source files for maximum compatibility. OKLCH provides perceptually uniform color manipulation, meaning contrast ratios remain consistent across the palette.

Token reference

For the complete list of available tokens:
Color tokens — See Foundations for the full color role reference
Typography tokens — Display, headline, title, body, and label scales
Spacing tokens — 4px–48px+ scale with CSS custom properties
Elevation tokens — Shadow definitions for each elevation level
State layer tokens — Hover (8%), focus (10%), pressed (10%), dragged (16%) opacity values
